bottle-green.note: The accent, replacing Stadium Amber. Reads as a mark (ink, a stamp) rather than a light source.

leaf-green.note: Hover/active shift of the accent; resting color of text links outside the footer.

ivory.note: Text/marks that sit ON the accent fill (buttons, badges, checkbox tick, footer text). Inverse of the old dark-theme 'Ink' token.

canvas.note: Flat page background, painted once on body/html. No gradient.

pine-black.note: The one deliberately dark surface — the footer. Structural equivalent of the old dark-theme Near Black.

error.note: Deepened from the old dark-theme #d64545 — that value reads ~4:1 on Canvas (below AA); this holds ~6.3:1. State color only, never an accent.

display.purpose: Hero headline only — one per page.

title.purpose: Card titles, step titles, accordion summaries.

body.purpose: Running copy, ~680px max width, Text Muted with Text Primary emphasis.

shadows.name: card-rest
shadows.purpose: The only resting shadow. Portfolio cards, to anchor them on the canvas. Green-tinted and soft — a flat black shadow reads harsh on light, paper-like ground.

shadows.name: button-lift
shadows.purpose: Green-tinted rise on primary button :hover, paired with translateY(-2px).

shadows.name: phone-drop
shadows.purpose: Grounds the floating phone mockup in 'O nas'.

shadows.name: step-target-ring
shadows.purpose: Bottle Green ring on a :target process step linked from the nav.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on every interactive element (outline, not box-shadow).

motion.name: ease-glide
motion.purpose: Default easing for every transition and keyframe animation (the --ease token).

motion.name: micro
motion.purpose: Nav link opacity, card-link gap, checkbox box transitions.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Shared IntersectionObserver scroll-in for content blocks (hero excluded — see hero-reveal).

motion.name: hero-reveal
motion.value: double requestAnimationFrame, then the standard 0.6s reveal transition with the same 90ms stagger
motion.purpose: Hero (and hero--compact) content is always in the initial viewport, so it reveals on load rather than via IntersectionObserver, which fires too early for already-visible elements to animate reliably.

motion.name: phone-reveal
motion.purpose: The longer glide on the 'O nas' phone figure as it slides in from lower-right.

motion.name: ambient-loop
motion.purpose: phone-float (img) and phone-glow (::before) idle loops, in sync.

components.name: Terminal Panel
components.description: Replaced the Floating Phone in 'O nas' on 22.09.2026 — same slot, same showpiece/signature-motion role. A small, self-contained dark card styled like a real code editor (own literal colors, not this system's tokens — see the Colors scoped-exception note in DESIGN.md): a macOS-style title bar with three status dots, then a fixed-height, edge-faded viewport showing a short looping CTA message. On the live page the content is duplicated once and the whole track animates translateY(0) -> translateY(-50%) for a seamless vertical loop (same trick as the Trainings Marquee, rotated 90deg); shown here as one static, non-looping copy — the live panel's full animation and prefers-reduced-motion handling live in style.css, not in this preview. The whole live figure is aria-hidden (it repeats nothing the adjacent text column doesn't already say).

components.name: Trainings Marquee
components.description: Infinite horizontal loop of 8 training-type icons + labels, between the hero and 'O nas' on the homepage. Two identical list copies sit in one flex track; the track animates translateX(0) -> translateX(-50%) on a 32s linear infinite loop — exactly one copy's width, so the wrap is seamless. The duplicate copy is aria-hidden so screen readers hear each label once. Icons are neutral (Text Primary); a small Bottle Green dot after each label is the only accent — a full row of solid-green icons would spend the One Mark Rule's scarcity on decoration. prefers-reduced-motion stops the animation and drops the hidden duplicate. Shown here as a static, non-looping preview with 3 of the 8 items (no duplicate list, no animation) — the live page has the full set and the loop.

narrative.overview:
FitPage now looks like a training space at first light: pale cream walls, the calm of early morning before the noise starts. The one deep note is Bottle Green (#1F3D2B) — not a light source anymore, but a mark: ink, a stamp, the color of a well-kept mat — and it touches almost nothing: the button to press, the link to follow, the number of the step you're on. Everything else is quiet, warm off-white. The register is exactly what it always was — focused and disciplined, never loud — just relit.

The page itself is one flat canvas (#F7F3EA), painted once on body. No gradient, no variation by scroll position — the same tone from the first pixel to the last. There is no card, no panel: content sits directly on the canvas, section rhythm built entirely from padding, not boxes. Depth is almost entirely absent at rest; shadows appear only when something lifts — a button on hover, the terminal panel grounded in 'O nas,' a handful of small component cards (portfolio, steps, form fields) that keep their own faint tinted fill. The one deliberately dark note left anywhere in the system is the footer — a near-black forest green, the single anchor at the bottom of an otherwise light page. A second, narrow dark note lives inside the terminal panel itself — a self-contained illustrative component, not a step toward a page theme.

Type now pairs Fraunces (600–700) for every heading against Inter (400–700) for body and UI chrome — a deliberate switch from the original native system-font stack, chosen to contrast on purpose: a wonky, characterful display serif against a neutral, highly legible grotesque. The restraint is still the point — the interface should feel engineered and calm so the trainer's own words and image are the loudest thing on screen.
keyCharacteristics: One accent (Bottle Green), on roughly 10% or less of any screen.
A flat cream canvas (#F7F3EA), painted once on body — no gradient, no per-section repaint.
Section rhythm is padding/margin only; no card, border, or box ever separates one section from the next.
Full 999px pills for actions; a 6 / 10 / 14px radius ladder for everything else.
Fraunces headings against an Inter body — a deliberately contrasting pair, not the earlier system-font stack.

Light-only for the page itself, by deliberate choice — not a default light/dark pairing. One narrow, disclosed exception: the decorative terminal panel in 'O nas' is its own small dark surface, not a site theme.
Motion gated behind .js and prefers-reduced-motion, always with a static fallback.

rules.name: The One Mark Rule
rules.body: Bottle Green appears on ~10% or less of any screen. It is for the single next action, links, focus, and step numbers — never a large fill and never a run of text. Its scarcity is the signal; it reads as ink, not illumination. Renamed from 'The One Lamp Rule' — the old dark world's accent was a light source, this one is a mark.

rules.name: The Flat Canvas Rule
rules.body: One solid color (#F7F3EA) is painted once, on body, and never varies by scroll position. No section carries a background of its own; content sits directly on the canvas, separated from its neighbours by padding alone. Never repaint a section opaque — the footer (Pine Black) is the sole deliberate exception. Replaces 'The Single Gradient Rule': the gradient is gone, but the underlying discipline — one background, painted once, sections never repaint it — survives intact.

rules.name: The System-Font Rule (superseded)
rules.body: Originally: do not load a web font to 'improve' the type — hierarchy comes from weight/tracking on the system stack, a custom face would fight its engineered character. Explicitly overturned by direct instruction: load Fraunces for headings and Inter for body. Kept on record, not deleted, so the reversal doesn't get rediscovered from git blame.

rules.name: The Lift-Means-Interactive Rule
rules.body: With the exception of the portfolio card's resting shadow, the terminal panel's constant grounding shadow, and the primary-CTA pulse, a shadow means the element is hovered or targeted. Resting surfaces read as flat, tinted paper.

rules.name: The CTA Pulse (exception)
rules.body: The three instances of the primary 'Umów konsultację' button — hero, .nav__cta, and the closing CTA on index.html — carry a continuous, ambient box-shadow pulse independent of hover/focus, specified in full detail by the site owner. A deliberate, narrow exception to Lift-Means-Interactive and to 'reserve motion for content that changes' — not a reflexive pattern. Gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; pauses on hover/focus.

rules.name: The Full Pill Rule
rules.body: Action elements (buttons, nav CTA) are full 999px pills. Everything else uses the 6 / 10 / 14px ladder. Do not mix radii within one component and do not give an action a boxy radius.

rules.name: Named Rule — no invented statistics
rules.body: The aggregate review summary must never show a rating number unmatched by a real review count behind it. With zero real reviews live, the summary shows outline stars and '0 opinii' — no numeric average at all, since a rating with nothing behind it is a fabricated statistic.

dos: Do keep the canvas flat — one solid color on body, no gradient, no per-section repaint.
Do separate sections with padding/margin only, never a box.

Do verify body and secondary text clears 4.5:1 on Canvas — and re-check independently anywhere a color sits on a different surface (the footer, the accent fill, a hover state); a pair that passes on Canvas can still fail elsewhere.
Do keep Bottle Green rare: the next action, links, focus rings, step numbers. Running copy stays Text Muted / Text Primary.
Do use full 999px pills for actions and the 6 / 10 / 14px ladder for every other corner.
Do gate every animation behind the .js class and prefers-reduced-motion, with the content fully visible and usable when both are off.
Do put a 2px Bottle Green focus outline (outline-offset: 1–2px) on every interactive element.
Do draw custom controls (checkbox, <details> markers, icons) from scratch in the light palette instead of styling native chrome.
Do define shapes with the hairline border — fills are almost invisible on their own.
donts: Don't ship the template look: no stock hero photo, no grid of identical rounded cards, no gradient-filled buttons. This is the one confirmed anti-reference.

Don't give a section its own background, border, blur, or radius of any kind — no panel, no card, no translucent fill. Sections are pure spacing. (The footer, #16211B, is the sole opaque exception, and the small component-level cards keep their own faint fill — neither is a section-level panel.)
Don't use Bottle Green for large fills or runs of text; its scarcity is the point.
Don't add a second accent hue. Green + neutral only; Error red (#A13333) is a state color, not an accent.

Don't introduce or assume a page dark theme. The system is light-only, by deliberate choice — this doesn't prohibit a single, disclosed, self-contained dark component (the terminal panel) that stays literal-colored and never becomes a reusable token or a toggle.
Don't load a web font to 'fix' the typography; weight and tracking carry the hierarchy.
Don't let a shadow sit on a resting surface (portfolio card excepted) — shadows mean hover, :target, or the animated phone.
Don't reuse the standard Leaf Green link color inside the footer — it fails contrast there (~2.6:1). Use Ivory.
